question_text: Firm Qualifications. Describe the firm's history, size, office locations and its work for special districts.
answer_text: Example Firm LLP is a public agency law firm. Our special district group serves as general counsel to water, fire, sanitary and recreation districts. For {AGENCY} the work would be led from our Stonemill office. Every client has one responsible partner, and that partner stays on the engagement.

question_text: Assigned Personnel. Name the lead attorney and other attorneys who would serve the District, and state each person's role. Attach resumes.
answer_text: We staff each engagement with a small team so that {AGENCY_SHORT} always speaks to someone who knows its matters. The lead attorney is responsible for all advice and attends {GOVERNING_BODY} meetings in person. The backup attorney is copied on open matters and can step in on short notice.

question_text: Work Plan. Describe how the firm would deliver the services in Section III, including meeting attendance, turnaround times and how the firm keeps the Board informed.
answer_text: We propose to serve {AGENCY} with one lead attorney who attends every regular {GOVERNING_BODY} meeting. Before each meeting we review the agenda with the {CHIEF_EXEC}. When {AGENCY_SHORT} considers new rates and charges we review the rate study before it goes to the {GOVERNING_BODY}.

question_text: Transition. Describe how the firm would take over from retiring counsel.
answer_text: We would meet retiring counsel in the first week, collect the open files and calendar every deadline. We would give the {GOVERNING_BODY} a written list of open matters with a recommended next step for each. This is the same plan we used for Kettle Bend Irrigation District.
